candidate: Declared relation/predicate resolver micro-oracle over strict ClayCode surface
expected_semantic_property: Human-readable relation/predicate forms may remain parseable only when the operator/predicate is explicitly declared and resolved into typed canonical IR; arbitrary identifier-as-operator syntax must fail closed.
counterhypothesis: Normalize all prose-like relation forms to punctuation/calls/qualified fields and forbid declared word operators entirely; this may yield lower parser complexity and repair cost.
falsifier: A full-current-corpus parser/roundtrip benchmark shows declared word-operator resolution causes ambiguity, materially higher repair cost, unstable semantic hashes, or worse target-reader/compiler performance than explicit normalization.
new_information_vs_existing_workers: The concurrent strict-syntax worker rejected arbitrary identifier-infix and proposed normalization. This experiment tests a narrower third option: a finite declared relation/predicate registry. It is not generic infix and not a production parser implementation.
release_effect: CC-WP-02 remains OPEN; candidate is eligible only for full-corpus cost/roundtrip comparison against normalization policy.
